## Scope

Consider any finite number of fixed-temperature terminals and internal thermal
stores. Every internal node v has a **constant positive scalar capacity** C_v.
Every edge has a bounded nonnegative reciprocal conductance g_uv(t)=g_vu(t),
piecewise continuous and periodic with finite period P. There is no advection,
coherent-wave interference, internal source, temperature-dependent controller,
capacity modulation or reset. Assume the averaged graph grounds every internal
component at a terminal, so the stable periodic solution is unique.

Let qbar=Y theta be its period-averaged terminal-current response, with current
positive into the network. Let G_union contain an edge exactly when its integrated
conductance over a period is positive. A terminal-avoiding path from i to j may
have arbitrary internal vertices, but no other terminal as an intermediate
vertex. Fixed-temperature terminals absorb a perturbation and are not transit
storage nodes.

Let I denote the set of internal vertices. The stage1 static-comparator theorems allow a general constant SPD storage matrix.
The result here requires diagonal positive capacities. This restriction is
essential to the positive-system proof and is not silently extended to the
larger algebraic class.

## Theorem

For any distinct terminals i and j:

1. Y_ji<=0.
2. Y_ji<0 if and only if there is a terminal-avoiding path from i to j in G_union.
3. In particular, Y_ji=0 if and only if Y_ij=0. The terminal response has exactly
   the same off-diagonal zero pattern as the static Kron reduction of the union
   graph, although its nonzero coefficients can be strongly unequal.

Consequently, a finite circuit in this class cannot have nonzero forward DC
transfer with exactly zero reverse DC transfer. Adding more finite stores,
more finite conductance phases or zero off-state contacts cannot change that
statement. It does not prohibit large **finite** isolation ratios.

There is a quantitative, generally conservative version. Let

\[
 i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_k,v_{k+1}=j
\]

be any terminal-avoiding simple path, with k internal vertices. Define

\]

## Q42: perfect isolation is blocked in the finite positive-contact class

I checked [REVERSE_TRANSFER_PROOF.md](../../review_material/Q42/stage2/REVERSE_TRANSFER_PROOF.md). With diagonal positive capacities, nonnegative variation of constants gives nonnegative internal response. A terminal-avoiding union-graph path can be traversed over successive repeated periods; bounded escape leaves a positive retained fraction. The chronological windows give the stated `exp(-k*delta*P)` floor, with one capacity factor per internal node. Reversing the same undirected path preserves the positive floor. If no such path exists, the corresponding unforced internal component stays at zero. This establishes the exact symmetric zero pattern and rules out finite forward transfer with exactly zero reverse transfer throughout the stated class.

The restriction excluding intermediate clamped terminals is necessary. My twelve independent sparse ODE cases include explicit terminal cuts, arbitrary phase order, and newly connected internal paths: cut pairs have zero response, connected pairs have strictly positive transfer in both directions and satisfy the floor. Four optimized ring circuits independently integrated with my ODE solver reproduce their recorded directional excesses within `3.22e-14`. Both stronger mechanisms remain below the one-body ordinary controller in the executed throughput searches; the long-period search is not a global impossibility proof for all approximate routers.

I also reproduce the consequential arithmetic failure: at `z=800`, Float64 gives reverse coefficient zero, while 100-digit arithmetic gives `1.528281076740703...e-351`; the finite isolation ratio is `2.726374572112566...e347`, and cooling is only `0.001875` of the matched static star. This is a false numerical zero, not perfect routing. The full 680-pair support/floor and 64-case SPD replays pass; the latter correctly demonstrates why general SPD storage cannot inherit positive thermal-compartment sign claims. The support replay emits the already preserved host BLAS warnings while returning finite consistent results.

The [Dörfler–Simpson-Porco–Bullo primary author text, Proposition 5.7](https://www.control.utoronto.ca/~jwsimpson/papers/2017k/) already supplies the static internal-path Kron criterion, and its compartmental discussion supplies established positivity antecedents. The periodic quant
